name: shared
note: version 4 (probe store_rider) lives on branch task/fg-store-dest and is not on main; this version extends protocol-v3.json
data_seen_before_writing: store_step r1 (protocol v3), free-running stores, cycles per store: one writer / per SM with four writers — 1 wavefront (32-bit, 32 words) 4.88 / 1.22 (b300), 5.00 / 1.25 (h100): bound by the issue interval, the SM cost is not observable; 4 wavefronts (128-bit, 32 words each) 12.76 / 4.72 and 15.51 (K = 4; contradicted by its own K = 8 cell) / 4.45; 16 wavefronts (128-bit 8 words, and 32-bit 2 words) 31.98 / 16.00 and 31.95 / 15.99 on both devices; 32 wavefronts (32-bit, 1 word) 63.87 / 31.97. Installed: per SM 1.0021 x wavefronts (b300), 1.0112 x (h100), affine; per SMSP linear knots 1 / 4 / 16 / 32. The per-SM cost at 4 wavefronts is 18 % (b300) / 10 % (h100) above the installed line; 2 and 8 wavefronts were never measured; wavefront width was only varied at 16 wavefronts (no effect). The engine truncates the per-SM cost to an integer. No cell of this version has been run.
question: Is the acceptance cost of a shared store a function of its wavefront count alone, and what is it at 1-8 wavefronts, per SMSP and per SM?
probe: probe/store_step.cu unchanged (tail 0: stores only, no barrier; one CTA, 4 warps, one per SMSP; one clock read before and after each warp's loop). The geometry sets the wavefront count w and the words per wavefront: 32-bit stores with lane stride 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 B give w = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 with 32 / 16 / 8 / 4 / 2 / 1 words; 128-bit stores with lane stride 16 / 32 / 64 / 128 B give w = 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 with 32 / 16 / 8 / 4 words.
cells: run_store_wave.sh: 10 geometries x K {4, 8} x writer mask {1, 3, 7, 15} = 80 cells per run, runs a and b, both devices. SASS gate: the store_step gate (36 kernels) unchanged.
definitions: u1(g) = period(mask 1) / K: per store on one SMSP. u4(g) = period(mask 15) / (4 K): per store on the SM. The SM cost is observable in a geometry only where period(mask 15) > 1.05 x period(mask 1); otherwise the SM does not bind and u4 is only an upper bound. K = 8 is the reference; K = 4 must agree within 3 % or the K = 8 value is used and the knot is experimental.
controls: The five geometries of r1 (32-bit stride 4 / 64 / 128, 128-bit stride 16 / 64) reproduce their r1 periods within 2 % on masks 1, 3, 15; runs a / b within 1 %.

hypotheses_declared_before_data.H_wf: the cost depends on the wavefront count only: at w = 4, 8, 16, 32 the 32-bit and the 128-bit geometry agree within max(3 %, 0.5 cycle) in u1 and (where observable) u4.
hypotheses_declared_before_data.H_width: it also depends on the words per wavefront: the two geometries differ beyond that bound at w = 4 or 8 (the 32-word wavefronts of the 128-bit store being dearer), as they do not at 16.
hypotheses_declared_before_data.installed_prediction: per SM 1.00 x w (4.0 at 4, 8.0 at 8); per SMSP by interpolation 7.2 at 2 and 19.2 at 8 (b300).

decision: H_wf: both leaves become linear tables over shared_wavefronts. Per-SM knots: every w where the SM cost is observable, value = mean of the available geometries at K = 8 (measured; experimental if K = 4 disagrees or the two devices' runs differ by more than 1 %); below the smallest observable w the installed slope x w is kept as a knot and marked as not re-measured. Per-SMSP knots at 2 and 8 are added and 4 is re-derived the same way. The engine keeps the fraction of the per-SM cost (as it already does per SMSP). H_width: nothing is installed; the table of both widths is recorded and a wavefront-width axis is proposed. Mixed (agree at 8, differ at 4): nothing installed. Full-GPU error is not used.
replay: before any full-GPU run the store_step captures (store-step-replay/cap-<device>, 17 cells) are replayed; the 4-wavefront free-running four-writer cell (hardware 75.4 / 71.3, engine 64.0) and the 4-wavefront fence rounds must move toward hardware and no 16-wavefront cell may move by more than 1 %.
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no hypothesis added after data without an addendum that says the data was seen.

addenda.name: result
addenda.after_run: store-wave b300-r1 (GPU-36989eed) and h100-r1 (GPU-8daa325d): 80 cells x 2 runs, SASS gate 36 / 36, runs identical, controls within 0.01 % of r1
addenda.declared_checks: H_wf holds at w = 8, 16, 32 (both widths agree to 0.1 %) and fails at w = 4 (128-bit 12.88 / 13.38 against 32-bit 8.00; per SM 4.75 / 4.12 against 4.00): the declared outcome is 'mixed' and nothing is installed from this run. Facts that stand on their own: per SMSP 2.00 x w and per SM 1.00 x w for w = 2..32 in every geometry but one; the exception is the 128-bit store that writes 512 contiguous bytes (four full 32-word wavefronts), which is the pattern of the GEMM epilogue. The installed per-SMSP table (protocol v3: knots 1 / 4 / 16 / 32 with 12.75 / 13.0 at 4) is right for that pattern only: a 4-wavefront 32-bit store costs 8.00 (table 12.75), 8 wavefronts cost 16.0 (interpolated 19.2), 2 wavefronts at most 4.88 (7.2).
addenda.hypothesis_after_data: H_bytes: a shared store costs max(per-wavefront cost x w, bytes written / data rate) on each of the two frontiers. From the one deviating geometry at K = 8: per SMSP 512 / 12.88 = 39.8 B per cycle (b300), 512 / 13.38 = 38.3 (h100); per SM 512 / 4.75 = 107.8 (b300), 512 / 4.12 = 124.3 (h100). Every other geometry writes at most 512 B over 8 or more wavefronts, or 128 B, and is wavefront-bound under H_bytes, so the run supports it with one point per device only.

addenda.name: bytes
addenda.text: Written before any 64-bit cell is run. Probe change: store_step gains WIDE 2 (st.shared.v2.b32, an 8-byte store per lane; kernels k_step<2, 4, 0, 0> and <2, 8, 0, 0>; the SASS gate requires K STS.64 in the loop). Cells (run_store_bytes.sh, 40 per run): 64-bit stores with lane stride 8 (2 full wavefronts, 256 B), 16 (4 wavefronts of 16 words, 256 B), 32 (8 wavefronts of 8 words); the 128-bit stride 16 and the 32-bit stride 16 geometries again as controls; K {4, 8} x mask {1, 3, 7, 15}. Predictions at K = 8. 64-bit stride 8: H_bytes per SMSP 256 / 39.8 = 6.44 (b300), 256 / 38.3 = 6.69 (h100); per SM 2.375 (b300), 2.06 (h100). 'Wavefronts only': per SMSP at the issue bound (4.88 / 5.00), per SM 2.00. 64-bit stride 16 and 32: 8.00 / 4.00 and 16.0 / 8.0 under both. Decision per device and frontier: H_bytes is accepted on the SMSP frontier if the stride-8 one-writer value is within 5 % of its prediction at K = 8 and within 8 % at K = 4, rejected if it is at most 5.2; on the SM frontier (b300 only; on h100 the two predictions are 3 % apart and the cell cannot decide) accepted if the four-writer value per store is within 3 % of 2.375, rejected if within 2 % of 2.00. Accepted on a frontier: that leaf gets cycles = the measured per-wavefront line (2.00 x w per SMSP, 1.00 x w per SM, knots at the measured w) and a data rate in bytes per cycle, the engine takes the larger; the h100 SM rate is installed as experimental from the 128-bit cell alone only if the b300 SM frontier is accepted. Rejected or unclear on a frontier: the installed leaf of that frontier is not changed in this round and the table is recorded. Full-GPU error is not used.

addenda.name: bytes_result
addenda.after_run: store-bytes b300-r1 (GPU-36989eed) and h100-r1 (GPU-9a626262): 40 cells x 2 runs (identical), SASS gate 38 / 38
addenda.text: Cycles per store at K = 8 (K = 4 in brackets), b300 / h100. 64-bit stride 8 (two full wavefronts, 256 B): one writer 8.01 (8.28) / 8.14 (9.54); four writers per SM 2.47 (2.50) / 2.50 (2.81). 64-bit stride 16 (4 wavefronts): 8.13 / 8.19 and 4.00 per SM; stride 32 (8 wavefronts): 16.0 and 8.00. Controls: 128-bit stride 16 12.88 / 13.38 and 4.75 / 4.12; 32-bit stride 16 8.00 and 4.00. Declared decision: on the SMSP frontier the stride-8 value is neither within 5 % of the H_bytes prediction (6.44 / 6.69) nor at the issue bound (<= 5.2); on the b300 SM frontier 2.47 is neither within 3 % of 2.375 nor within 2 % of 2.00. Both 'unclear': H_bytes is not accepted and nothing is installed from this run.

addenda.name: width
addenda.written: after seeing the store-wave and store-bytes data, before any cell of this addendum is run
addenda.text: Reading of the 20 one-writer geometries so far (both devices, K = 8): a shared store costs its SMSP max(2.00 x w, c(width)) with c(32-bit) at most 4.88 (the installed issue interval is 4.39 / 4.42), c(64-bit) about 8.0-8.1, c(128-bit) about 12.9 (b300) / 13.4 (h100); per SM 1.00 x w. H_width: c depends on the store's operand width, not on the bytes it writes. Probe change: --lanes N lets only the first N lanes of each writer warp store (same loop, the store predicate also tests the lane). Cells (run_store_width.sh, 30 per run): (1) 128-bit stride 16, 16 lanes (256 contiguous bytes, 2 wavefronts), K {4, 8}, mask {1, 15}; (2) 64-bit stride 8, 16 lanes (128 B, 1 wavefront), same; (3) 128-bit stride 16, 8 lanes (128 B, 1 wavefront), same; (4) 128-bit stride 24, 32 lanes (4 full wavefronts, not contiguous), same; (5) 128-bit stride 16, 32 lanes, mask 1, K {1, 2, 4, 8}: the per-store slope; (6) controls with 32 lanes: 128-bit stride 16 and 64-bit stride 8, K 8, mask {1, 15}; (7) 128-bit stride 16, 16 lanes, mask {3, 7}, K 8. Predictions for one writer at K = 8: H_width: (1) and (3) and (4) equal the 32-lane 128-bit value of the device (12.9 / 13.4) within 5 %, (2) equals the 32-lane 64-bit value (8.0 / 8.1) within 5 %. A cost that follows the bytes written instead gives (1) about 8.0, (2) and (3) at most 5.2. Decision: H_width is accepted on a device if (1), (2), (3), (4) are all within 5 % of the H_width prediction; then storage.shared.acceptance_smsp is partitioned by the operand width (width_bytes 4 / 8 / 16) and each leaf is a linear table over shared_wavefronts that represents max(2.00 x w, c(width)) with c from the K = 8 one-writer cells of this and the two earlier runs (32-bit: the installed issue interval; measured where K = 4 and K = 8 agree within 3 %, else experimental). The per-SM leaf is not changed (1.00 x w is what the runs show where the SM binds with four writers; the extra 0.5-3 cycles per store when the SMSP pacing meets a nearly saturated SM are recorded, not modelled). If any of (1)-(4) is within 5 % of the bytes prediction instead, or outside both, nothing is installed. Full-GPU error is not used.

addenda.name: width_result
addenda.after_run: store-width b300-r1 (GPU-36989eed) and h100-r1 (GPU-9a626262): SASS gate 38 / 38, 22 cells x 2 runs measured (identical); the four cells of group (4) failed on both devices with the CUDA error 'misaligned address'
addenda.cell_4: A 128-bit shared store needs a 16-byte aligned address; a 24-byte lane stride cannot be executed. The cell was a design error of this addendum and cannot be realised on hardware. The acceptance condition is therefore read on (1), (2), (3) only; this relaxation is written after seeing them.
addenda.result: One writer, cycles per store at K = 8, b300 / h100, next to the 32-lane control of the same binary: (1) 128-bit, 16 lanes (256 B, 2 wavefronts) 12.63 / 13.26, control 12.63 / 13.26; (3) 128-bit, 8 lanes (128 B, 1 wavefront) 12.63 / 13.26; (2) 64-bit, 16 lanes (128 B, 1 wavefront) 7.76 / 8.02, control 7.76 / 8.02. The predictions that follow the bytes written (8.0, at most 5.2, at most 5.2) are refuted; H_width holds exactly. (5) 128-bit one-writer period at K = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8: 26.0 / 35.0 / 51.0 / 101.0 (b300), 30.4 / 36.0 / 60.0 / 106.1 (h100; about 14 + 11.5 K, which is why the h100 K = 4 and K = 8 values per store differ). Four writers, per store on the SM at K = 8: 128-bit 16 lanes 4.19 / 4.68, 8 lanes 5.16 / 4.72, 32 lanes 4.72 / 4.28; 64-bit 16 lanes 2.41 / 2.47: the SM frontier has a width-dependent floor too (about 4.2-5.2 for 128-bit, 2.4-2.5 for 64-bit, at most 1.22 for 32-bit), unsteady by +-12 % across K and lane count; by the declaration the per-SM leaf is not changed in this round.
addenda.installed: storage.shared.acceptance_smsp partitioned by width_bytes; each leaf a linear table over shared_wavefronts for max(2.00 x w, c). c at K = 8 over the three runs: 128-bit b300 12.88 / 12.88 / 12.63 -> 12.80 (K = 4: 12.76; measured), h100 13.38 / 13.38 / 13.26 -> 13.34 (K = 4: 15.0-15.5; experimental); 64-bit b300 8.01 / 7.76 -> 7.89 (experimental), h100 8.14 / 8.02 -> 8.08 (experimental); 32-bit: the installed issue interval (4.388 / 4.415). The 2.00 x w line is measured at w = 4, 8, 16, 32 (32-bit), 8, 16, 32 (128-bit) and 4, 8 (64-bit); 64-bit at 16 and 32 and every width at 3, 5-7 take the line without a cell. Stores narrower than 32 bits use the 32-bit leaf (not measured).
addenda.not_installed: the per-SM width floor; the 0.5-3 cycles per store lost when SMSP-paced stores meet a nearly saturated SM (two writers +1..2, three writers +1.0, four writers 0 for wavefront-bound stores).
